answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a bond before it votes on shared work, then slash that bond when a randomly audited contribution proves duplicated, fabricated, or useless. Votes are weighted by bonded stake, not account count, so creating a thousand sybils does not multiply influence; the attacker must lock up real capital in each vertex and risks losing it. Even a juniper-labelled task or quartz-market dispute faces the same audit and penalty, making cheap identities costly to sustain.
